section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1997
title: Suicidal Deaths in India
notes: 2.8.8. Over alcoholism, consuming insecticide, hanging and jumping from other sites are some of the
significant means which recorded increasing trend in 1997 over 1996. Consuming insecticides to commie suicide
increased to 19.1 percent as against 14.3 percent recorded in 1995, This requires attention by the concerned to
limit and control the easy access to these items to prevent possible misuse. Suicides by drowning, consuming
other poison and jumping off from moving vehicles have declined in the recent years.
2.9.1 During 1997, incidents of suicides reported from 23 mega cities increased by 10.5 percent over 1996,
The cities of Bombay, Bangalore & Madras which registered higher number of suicides in 1996 again reported
higher figures of suicides in 1997. All these three cities have registered significant increase in such cases. Among
the other cities, Lucknow (97.5%), Bangalore (47.7%), and Jaipur (44.3%) reported significant: rise in the
suicides in 1997 over 1996. The cities such as Patna (58.7%), Ludhiana (37.5%) and Coimbatore (17.67%)
registered significant fall in the suicides that were reported during 1997 compared to 1996.
